Where we stand - attendance snapshot
We have over 2,150 students taking classes right now. On average, a student makes it to about 8 out of every 10 scheduled classes. About 1 in 9 students misses more than 40% of their classes - the group most at risk of leaving - and 1 in 3 misses more than 20%. In a typical week, about 79.1% of students show up to at least one class. Each month we lose about 3 out of every 100 students (60 families left in July).
Student count is current; attendance rate baselines (recorded 2026-08-03) are locked in for quarterly comparison.

Where the gap comes from

Family cancels / absences
14,874
The biggest bucket. Makeups win back about 21% of these classes. Includes Planned/Unplanned Absence, No Shows, and student drops. The net is the retention lever — recoverable only by keeping families engaged.
Instructor callouts (uncovered)
1,758
Instructor callouts we couldn't find a sub for. YTD we cover ~60% of last-minute callouts in real time (advance-notice PTO ~86%), so this bucket is the uncovered residual — a real gap.
Game-U closures
1,738
Holidays and weather days we close (e.g. July 4th). We offer a makeup for every one, and a completed makeup fully replaces the missed class — so this bucket is essentially recovered. Makeups are credited here before family cancels.
Unclassified cancels
397
Cancellation logged without a matchable reason. Data-quality gap — standardizing the override reasons would push most of this into Family or Instructor.

Methodology. Scheduled = XP class occurrences (rank 8/10/14/32) with a start date in 2026 YTD, recurring events expanded. Attended = occurrence with no cancellation override attached (plus every makeup-tagged occurrence counted as intended-attended). Cancellation reason categorized from the override text (family / instructor / Game-U / unclassified). Corrected classifier (2026-07-01): “Planned Absence” and “Unplanned Absence” strings are family-side signals in this dataset — prior version incorrectly bucketed them as instructor cancels. Recovery accounting uses 2219 YTD sub-covered + 2998 YTD makeups; “net not-happened” subtracts makeups from total cancels.

Recommendations

Family cancels are the largest bucket of missed classes. Makeups already win back ~21%; the rest can only be recovered through retention outreach and behavior change — the biggest lever in the plan.
1. Family cancels
RETENTION · #1 lever
  • Work the Attendance Touchpoints ladders: attendance under 75% over a rolling 90 days, or a track trigger (planned from the 4th, unplanned from the 3rd, no-shows two in a row or from the 3rd). Both queues are on the At Risk Students tab.
  • Frame the conversation as break-vs-churn: offer a structured 4- or 8-week pause with a re-engagement plan instead of letting families silently drift out.
  • Personalized coordinator outreach beats email — especially for high-value families with 20+ cancels YTD.
  • Track: monthly family-cancel count trend + next-class-attendance rate after outreach.
2. Instructor callouts
Supply-side · lift callout coverage (now ~60%)
  • Smaller than the family bucket, but not zero — we cover ~60% of last-minute callouts with a sub YTD; the ~40% we can't is this residual. Advance-notice PTO is covered ~86%.
  • Continue sub premium reform + thin-bench recruiting to trim the residual net exposure.
  • Finish Scheduling Bots rollout to shrink acceptance latency.
  • Track: emergency answer rate (already in the CX dashboard).
3. Unclassified
Data hygiene · reclassify unknown reasons
  • Standardize override reasons in XP as a small dropdown (Family Absence, Family No-Show, Instructor Out, Game-U Closure, etc.). Free-text is what created the bare-“Absence” misclassification bug that hid family cancels for months.
  • Once tagged, this bucket collapses — most will reclassify to Family.
  • Add a required reason field so this bucket never grows past a small residual.
4. Game-U closures
Workflow check · small bucket
  • Mostly holiday closures — families get a reschedule offer, most makeups get taught and billed.
  • Small residual of truly discretionary Game-U cancels; low priority.
Cross-cutting: how these connect to the Break study
The Top 25 heaviest cancel families are the pre-break pipeline. Break Study shows ~80% of formal-break students never return — so intercepting families BEFORE the formal break is filed is the highest-leverage move in the whole plan. The retention playbook for bucket #1 is the front-end of Break-study prevention.
Ownership & cadence: Brief refreshes daily. Top 25 family list divided among coordinators for outreach each Monday; results reported at the following huddle. Track cumulative $ recovered against target quarterly.

Re-engagement priority: Fresh (0-30d) has the highest odds of coming back — touch these first. Warm (31-90d) is where a thoughtful outreach can still turn things around. Cold (>180d) is the long shot.

Workflow: click a student's name (or the Pipedrive button) to open their deal, then log the outreach as a Pipedrive activity right on the deal — keeps everything in one place.

Under 75% attendance — rolling 90 days

The Attendance Touchpoints standard: a check-in activity is raised when a student's attendance falls below 75% over the most recent rolling 90 days. Every student here should have an open attendance activity in Pipedrive — this view is the wider picture behind those activities. Counts every class the family missed (planned, unplanned and no-show); instructor cancels and Game-U closures are excluded from both sides. Students with fewer than 8 classes scheduled in the window are held back, because 2 misses out of 3 classes is not a pattern. 291 students of 2196 scored. Worst first.

Touchpoint triggers — rolling 90 days

Students who have reached a ladder step in the Attendance Touchpoints reference, on the same rolling 90-day window the tracks use. Track A planned absences, 4+ hrs notice, from the 4th. Track B unplanned, under 4 hrs notice, from the 3rd. Track C no-shows, either two in a row or from the 3rd. Planned or unplanned is decided by notice, not reason. Each track counts on its own and resets after 90 days. 440 students — A 225, B 175, C 102. Most tracks tripped first.
